textos: More than half of Vienna lives in subsidised housing. What about your city?
1869: on the Ring, the liberal bourgeoisie builds its palaces of rental flats.
Theophil Hansen: 100 × 50 metres in eight modules of 25, each with its own courtyard.
The courtyards merge and stop being light wells. One façade for several owners.
1919: the Social Democrats win Vienna. They decide on 25,000 homes in 1923 and 35,000 in 1927.
Karl Ehn (1927 – 1930): 1,382 homes in more than a kilometre.
It covers only 18% of the site: the rest is courtyards with laundries, kindergartens and a library.
For architect Carmen Díez Medina, the Palais Hansen would be the direct ancestor of these “palaces for the people”.
Ehn and his generation trained under Otto Wagner, in the urbanism of imperial Vienna.
In February 1934, the army shells the Hof with artillery.
Vienna has 220,000 municipal flats and another 200,000 subsidised co-op flats.
